# A Primer on Search Relevance

By Rolling Edition, with AI · **Foundations** · [Read it free online](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance)

[![The latest edition's stamp](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/stamp.svg)](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance) [![Checks](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-primer-on-search-relevance/actions/workflows/checks.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rollingedition/book-primer-on-search-relevance/actions/workflows/checks.yml)

How search engines find and rank results, and how to measure whether a change helps: lexical, semantic and hybrid retrieval, reranking with learned models and LLMs, and judgments from people and LLMs, on a real product catalog.

**Written with AI. Verified by people.** [How we make books](https://rollingedition.com/policies/editorial) · [Check a copy](https://rollingedition.com/check)

## Who it's for

For readers comfortable with Python, pandas and NumPy who are new to search: a data scientist or engineer asked to improve a search box, or to build retrieval for an LLM application.

## Contents

| | Chapter | By the end, you can | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Search, end to end](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/search-end-to-end) · [source](chapters/01-search-end-to-end.md) | build a rough but complete search pipeline for a product catalog, from a shopper's query to an ordered list of products, and measure with one number whether a change to that pipeline helps | 11 |
| 2 | [What relevance means](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/what-relevance-means) · [source](chapters/02-what-relevance-means.md) | read a set of relevance judgments critically: say what each grade claims about a product, find where the judgments came from and where they have holes, and decide how far to trust a score computed from them | 10 |
| 3 | [Measuring search](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/measuring-search) · [source](chapters/03-measuring-search.md) | compute the standard ranking metrics from scratch, check them against scikit-learn, choose one before you compare rankers, and tell whether the gap between two rankers on your test queries is established or could be chance | 12 |
| 4 | [Judgments from people and LLMs](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/judgments-from-people-and-llms) · [source](chapters/04-judgments-from-people-and-llms.md) | write judging guidelines, measure how well two judges agree with kappa and weighted kappa, read an LLM judge's errors from a confusion matrix, and decide where LLM judgments can stand in for people's and where they can't | 11 |
| 5 | [Lexical retrieval](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/lexical-retrieval) · [source](chapters/05-lexical-retrieval.md) | build lexical search from scratch: turn product text into terms, index the terms, and score products with TF-IDF and BM25, matching the bm25s library score for score | 13 |
| 6 | [Semantic retrieval](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/semantic-retrieval) · [source](chapters/06-semantic-retrieval.md) | build semantic retrieval for a catalog from stored embeddings: compare vectors by cosine similarity, find a query's nearest products exactly with NumPy, switch to an approximate index when a catalog outgrows exact search and measure what the index misses, and find the queries where embeddings go wrong | 16 |
| 7 | [Hybrid retrieval](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/hybrid-retrieval) · [source](chapters/07-hybrid-retrieval.md) | combine a lexical and a semantic ranking into one, either by adding normalized scores or by reciprocal rank fusion, tune how much each ranking counts on train queries, and decide with a paired test on test queries whether the combination beats the better of its two inputs | 12 |
| 8 | [Understanding queries](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/understanding-queries) · [source](chapters/08-understanding-queries.md) | change a shopper's query before retrieval: correct its spelling, write its units one way, expand it with synonyms, predict its product class, rewrite it with a large language model, search with a product that model imagines, and turn a follow-up into a standalone query | 12 |
| 9 | [Ranking](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/ranking) · [source](chapters/09-ranking.md) | describe each product that retrieval returns with features, train a learning-to-rank model with LightGBM on your own judgments, rerank the top of the list with a cross-encoder or an LLM, measure an LLM reranker's positional bias, set the rerank depth by counting its costs, and distil a slow reranker into a fast one | 14 |
| 10 | [Retrieval for LLM applications](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/retrieval-for-llm-applications) · [source](chapters/10-retrieval-for-llm-applications.md) | measure the retrieval behind an LLM that answers from it: score an answer by the products it cites, check each citation against what retrieval returned, measure the products the LLM reads, choose what to index as one retrievable unit, and read an agent's searches from the record of its tool calls | 10 |
| 11 | [Testing changes](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/testing-changes) · [source](chapters/11-testing-changes.md) | decide whether a change to search should ship: diff two rankers' results query by query, keep your test queries from flattering a change, size an A/B test, and compare two rankers by interleaving their results | 11 |

## Run the examples

Every example runs offline, in a pinned environment, and its output must match the book's. With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```sh
uv venv --python 3.12.15
uv pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
cd examples && ../.venv/bin/python load-the-store.py
```

Model outputs are recorded once in `examples/data/recorded/`, each folder with a `manifest.json` that names the model, its exact version and the script that recorded it, so the examples never call a model. `recordings/` holds the scripts that record them again.

Where the data comes from, and its licence: [`examples/data/wands/README.md`](examples/data/wands/README.md).

## How this book stays current

When a library this book uses releases a new version, every example runs again in the new version. Agents draft any fix and check every change, and a change merges once its checks pass; one with a serious risk, such as a security or copyright problem, waits for a Rolling Edition maintainer. Anyone can check the book or correct it with a pull request. Each new edition is stamped with its date, its examples passing and what changed. [See what changed in each edition](https://rollingedition.com/primer-on-search-relevance/changes).
